correctness.rationale: In the canonical Euclidean zero-sum model r_i=e_i-e_(i+1), the remaining path roots b_j=r_(j+1) have tridiagonal Gram G=diag(2)+offdiag(-1) and r_1=-sum b_j. For each n, the stated positive weights s sum to one; q=-sum s_j b_j belongs to Q_n, y=r1-q=-sum(1-s_j)b_j, h_j=(G(1-s))_j. Exact rational reconstruction independently checked every claimed contact support inequality for n=3..50: min h>=0, h_j=lambda on s_j>0 and h_j<=lambda otherwise, while <y,-r1> is smaller. Thus (r1-q)·(z-q)<=0 for every surviving vertex, a complete KKT projection certificate. The squared norm v^T Gv is 1/2,4/5,9/10 for n=3,4,5 and identically 11/12 for n>=6; supports sizes 2,3,4,4. The displayed algebraic support formulas prove these facts for all n, and affine independence of path roots proves the exposed face count. Finally distance-to-convex-set is convex, giving directed Hausdorff equality. No nonorthogonal unimodular coordinate change is used.
